q: How many pairs of spinal nerves do you have, and how are they divided?
options: 31 pairs: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 2 coccygeal
31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal
12 pairs: one for each thoracic vertebra

q: Order the connective tissue layers of a nerve from the outside in, ending with what they wrap.
A surgeon cuts across a nerve and sees several round bundles, each with its own sleeve. Which layer forms the sleeve around each bundle?
A surgeon cuts the right L5 dorsal root to relieve pain, leaving the ventral root intact. Predict the change in each variable on the right side, compared with before surgery.

variables.name: Action potentials reaching the L5 dorsal horn from the L5 dermatome
Sensation over the top of the right foot (L5 dermatome)
Motor commands leaving the cord through the L5 ventral root
Strength of ankle dorsiflexion when the person tries

q: After a fracture of the middle of the humerus, a patient cannot extend his wrist or fingers; his hand hangs limply when he holds his arm out, palm down. Which nerve is most likely injured?

A data-entry clerk wakes at night with numbness and tingling in her thumb, index and middle fingers. Her little finger feels normal, and her thumb is weak when she pinches. Pressure on which nerve best explains this?
options: Axillary nerve where it wraps the humerus
Median nerve in the carpal tunnel

q: You bang the inside of your elbow on a table edge and feel a jolt of tingling shoot into your little finger. Which nerve did you hit?
A soccer player is kicked hard on the outer side of the knee, just below the joint. Afterward his toes drag when he walks, and he lifts his knee high with each step. Which nerve was injured?
After a diving accident, a young man cannot grip with his hands or move his trunk or legs, yet he breathes on his own using his diaphragm. Which level of cord injury best fits?
Which statements about the rami of spinal nerves are correct? Select all that apply.
options: The dorsal ramus supplies the deep back muscles and the skin of the back
The ventral rami supply the limbs
Rami carry motor axons but no sensory axons
The thoracic ventral rami form the intercostal nerves
The brachial plexus is formed from dorsal rami

q: Fill the gap in the organization of the brachial plexus, from the cord outward: roots → trunks → ____ → cords → terminal branches.
In the figure, which spinal nerve supplies the skin at marker 6, the navel?

q: In the figure, which spinal nerve supplies the skin at marker 2, the tip of the thumb?

fig.alt: Front view of a body outline in anatomical position, palms facing forward, with ten numbered markers on dermatome landmarks. 1: the outer side of the right upper arm. 2: the tip of the right thumb. 3: the tip of the right middle finger. 4: the tip of the left little finger. 5: the chest at the level of the nipples. 6: the navel. 7: the right groin. 8: the inner side of the left leg just below the knee. 9: the top of the right foot near the big toe. 10: the outer edge of the left foot near the little toe.

q: A patient reports numbness only at marker 10 in the figure, the outer edge of the foot near the little toe. Which dorsal root is most likely affected?

fig.alt: Front view of a body outline in anatomical position, palms facing forward, with ten numbered markers on dermatome landmarks. 1: the outer side of the right upper arm. 2: the tip of the right thumb. 3: the tip of the right middle finger. 4: the tip of the left little finger. 5: the chest at the level of the nipples. 6: the navel. 7: the right groin. 8: the inner side of the left leg just below the knee. 9: the top of the right foot near the big toe. 10: the outer edge of the left foot near the little toe.

q: A surgeon cuts one thoracic dorsal root, T8, to treat pain. Afterward, the T8 band of skin feels slightly dull but is not numb. What best explains this?
options: Neighboring dermatomes overlap, so T7 and T9 still supply part of the T8 band
The T8 ventral root carries enough sensory axons to take over
The dorsal root ganglion was left intact, so its neurons still send signals into the cord
Sensory axons regrow through the cut root within hours
misconception: one dorsal root alone supplies each dermatome

q: A 70-year-old develops a painful, blistering rash in a band that starts at his spine on the right, wraps around his side and ends at his navel. The rash never crosses the midline. Where has the virus been lying dormant?
options: In the right T10 dorsal root ganglion
In the right T10 ventral horn
In the skin cells of the rash

q: This path of a sensory signal from the skin of the sole of the foot to the spinal cord has one wrong step. Find it.
options: Sensory ending in the skin of the sole
Sacral plexus and a ventral ramus
Dorsal root ganglion and dorsal root

q: A fall onto the shoulder fractures the surgical neck of the humerus. A week later the patient cannot lift his arm out to the side, and the skin over the outer shoulder is numb. Which nerve was damaged?
Why is every spinal nerve a mixed nerve?
options: It forms where a sensory dorsal root and a motor ventral root join
Each of its axons carries signals in both directions
It contains both myelinated and unmyelinated axons
It carries both somatic and autonomic axons

q: Marcus has burning pain from his buttock down the back of his thigh to the outer edge of his foot, a numb little toe, and weak push-off onto his toes. His knee extension is normal. Which structure is most likely compressed?
options: The femoral nerve in the femoral triangle
The common fibular nerve at the knee

q: Name the pinned nerve.

Two slender bulb-tipped nerves lie under the frontal lobes, an X-shaped crossing of two thick nerves sits behind them, and the remaining roots emerge in order down the midbrain, pons and medulla, the last ones as rows of small rootlets along the medulla and a long root running up beside it.

q: Which cranial nerves are purely sensory? Select all that apply.
Put these cranial nerves in numerical order, lowest number first.

A woman wakes to find the whole left side of her face slack: her left brow will not lift, her left eye will not close, and her mouth droops on the left. Touch on her left cheek feels normal. Which nerve is affected?
misconception: the facial nerve carries sensation from the face

q: After a head injury, a man’s right eye rests turned down and out. His right upper lid droops, and the dark opening at the center of his right eye stays wide when a light shines on it. Which nerve is damaged?
A patient sticks out his tongue and it points to the right. Which nerve is most likely damaged?
A patient sees double only when looking to his left. When he tries, his left eye cannot turn outward past the midline. Which nerve is affected?
After surgery to remove a lymph node from the side of her neck, a woman’s right shoulder droops, and she cannot shrug it fully or raise her arm above her head. Which nerve was injured?
Which cranial nerve carries most of the body’s parasympathetic axons, including those that slow the heart?
Which are functions of the vagus nerve? Select all that apply.
options: Moving the muscles of the voice box
Carrying sensory signals from the stomach to the brainstem
Increasing the activity of the stomach and intestines

q: A dentist injects anesthetic near a branch of the maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve. Which area goes numb?
options: The cheek, upper lip and upper teeth
The lower lip, chin and lower teeth
The front two-thirds of the tongue, for taste

q: An examiner touches a wisp of cotton to the surface of a patient’s left eye: neither eye blinks. Touching the right eye makes both eyes blink. Which nerve is most likely damaged?
Fill the gap in the gag response: touch at the back of the throat → ____ carries the signal in → medulla oblongata → vagus nerve → throat muscles contract.
This list pairs each cranial nerve with a function. One pairing is wrong. Find it.
Which three cranial nerves leave the skull together through the jugular foramen?
After a fall onto the front of his head, a cook finds that food tastes flat and he cannot smell coffee brewing. Which nerve was most likely damaged, and where?
options: Optic nerve, in the optic canal
Olfactory nerve, at the cribriform plate
Facial nerve, in the temporal bone
Trigeminal nerve, at the foramen rotundum

q: An older woman reports double vision when she reads or walks down stairs, and she tilts her head to reduce it. Her upper lids and the centers of her eyes look normal. Which nerve is most likely affected?
Which cranial nerves carry parasympathetic axons? Select all that apply.
Which nerve carries taste from the front two-thirds of the tongue?

A patient’s voice has become hoarse. When she says "ah", the back of the roof of her mouth rises on the left but stays low on the right, and the small hanging tag at the back of her mouth is pulled toward the left. Which nerve is damaged?
Name the pinned structure in the brainstem.

fig.alt: Two side-by-side drawings of a pathway from the right side of the body to the brain, each with a slice of spinal cord at the bottom, slices of medulla and midbrain above it, and a slice of cerebral hemisphere at the top. Left: a pink sensory neuron enters the back of the cord through a ganglion and climbs on the same side in a bundle at the back of the cord to the medulla; a second, teal neuron crosses there and rises to a relay in the thalamus; a third, purple neuron runs to the gyrus behind the central sulcus. Right: the pink neuron ends as soon as it enters the cord, the teal neuron crosses at once and climbs in a bundle on the opposite side of the cord to the thalamus, and a purple neuron again runs to the cortex.

q: Put the steps of the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway in order, for vibration felt on the left index finger.
options: A lamellated corpuscle in the fingertip depolarizes, firing action potentials
The first-order axon passes its cell body in a cervical dorsal root ganglion and enters the cord
The axon climbs, without synapsing, in the left fasciculus cuneatus
It synapses in the nucleus cuneatus of the medulla oblongata
The second-order axon crosses the midline and rises in the right medial lemniscus
A third-order neuron in the right thalamus projects to the right postcentral gyrus

q: Name the pinned tract in the spinal cord.

fig.alt: Two side-by-side drawings of a pathway from the right side of the body to the brain, each with a slice of spinal cord at the bottom, slices of medulla and midbrain above it, and a slice of cerebral hemisphere at the top. Left: a pink sensory neuron enters the back of the cord through a ganglion and climbs on the same side in a bundle at the back of the cord to the medulla; a second, teal neuron crosses there and rises to a relay in the thalamus; a third, purple neuron runs to the gyrus behind the central sulcus. q: A stab wound cuts the left half of the spinal cord at T10. Below the injury, which pattern of sensory loss do you expect?
options: All sensation lost on the left side only
All sensation lost on the right side only
Pain and temperature lost on the left; vibration and position lost on the right side
Vibration and position lost on the left; pain and temperature lost on the right
misconception: all sensory pathways cross at the same level

q: Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which binds a channel protein on certain free nerve endings, the same channel that opens with painful heat. Which type of sensory receptor does capsaicin stimulate?
You press a fingertip lightly, then press the same spot twice as hard. Predict the change in each variable in one tactile sensory neuron, compared with the light press.

variables.name: Size of the graded receptor potential in the ending
Height of each action potential
Number of action potentials per second
Number of nearby sensory neurons firing

q: A dentist injects a local anesthetic that blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in the nerve to a lower tooth, partway along its length. The tooth is then drilled. Predict the change in each variable, compared with no anesthetic.

variables.name: Receptor potentials in the nociceptor endings in the tooth
Action potentials reaching the brainstem from the tooth
Pain perceived from the tooth

q: You feel your socks when you first put them on, but a minute later you no longer notice them. What best explains this?
options: The socks stop pressing on the skin once the fabric warms up and stretches to fit
Rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors stop firing while the pressure holds steady
Nociceptors in the skin become exhausted
The dorsal columns stop conducting after a minute

q: A sprained ankle keeps hurting for hours while you sit still, instead of fading like the feel of a ring on your finger. Why?
options: Nociceptors are tonic and keep firing while the stimulus lasts
Pain travels in the dorsal columns, which do not adapt
Nociceptors are encapsulated endings with thick capsules
The thalamus blocks signals from the ring but not from the ankle

q: A 60-year-old man has crushing pain that spreads down the inner side of his left arm during a heart attack. His arm is healthy. What best explains why he feels pain in his arm?
options: Nerves from the heart run down the arm
Blood backs up into the arm and stretches its vessels
Heart and arm pain axons converge on the same dorsal horn neurons
The phrenic nerve carries heart pain up to the C3 to C5 dermatomes of the shoulder

q: After a fall from a bike, a teenager has blood collecting in the abdomen under the left side of the diaphragm. She complains of pain at the tip of her left shoulder, which is uninjured. Which spinal segments explain this?

Daniel has lost pain and temperature sensation across both shoulders and arms, but fine touch and vibration there are normal. A cavity has formed in the center of his cervical spinal cord. Why is only pain and temperature affected?
options: The cavity has destroyed both dorsal columns along the back of the cord
The cavity presses on the dorsal root ganglia
Nociceptors in the arms have died
Crossing spinothalamic axons pass just in front of the central canal

q: A blocked artery damages the lateral part of the left medulla oblongata. The patient has lost pain and temperature on the left side of the face and on the right side of the body. How does one small area of damage cause loss on opposite sides?
options: Its uncrossed face pain axons run beside already crossed body pain axons
Both pathways cross at the medulla, so both losses should be on the right side
The left facial nerve and the right spinal nerves were both damaged
The dorsal columns cross in the medulla and carry pain from both sides

q: Which sensations travel in the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway? Select all that apply.
In the spinothalamic tract, where does the second-order axon cross the midline?
options: In the medulla oblongata, at the same level where the dorsal column axons cross
In the spinal cord, within a segment or two of where the signal entered

q: Fill the gap in the pain pathway from the right hand: nociceptor → first-order neuron → synapse in the right dorsal horn → ____ → left thalamus → third-order neuron → left primary somatosensory cortex.
options: First-order axon rising in the right dorsal column
Second-order axon crossing and rising in the left spinothalamic tract
Second-order axon rising on the same side in the right medial lemniscus
Third-order axon crossing in the medulla

q: This description of the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway for the right foot has one wrong step. Find it.
options: A tactile corpuscle in the right sole fires action potentials
The first-order axon enters through a sacral dorsal root
The first-order axon synapses in the right dorsal horn
The axon climbs in the right fasciculus gracilis
The second-order axon crosses in the medulla into the left medial lemniscus
A third-order neuron runs from the left thalamus to the left postcentral gyrus

q: Sensory endings in the wall of the urinary bladder fire as it fills and stretches. How are they classified?
Sensory receptors in your arteries report your blood pressure to the brainstem every second, yet you never feel your blood pressure. Which statement explains this?
options: These sensory receptors adapt completely within seconds
The signals are a sensation that does not become a perception
Blood pressure signals travel in the dorsal columns, which do not reach awareness
Blood pressure signals are blocked in the spinal cord

q: A woman cannot feel a vibrating tuning fork on either ankle and cannot tell whether her big toe is being moved up or down. Pain and temperature in her legs are normal, and she sways when she stands with her eyes closed. Where is the damage most likely?
options: Both dorsal columns of the spinal cord

q: A small bleed damages the right thalamus. Which pattern of sensory loss is expected?
options: Right side of the body only, all sensations
Fine touch on the right, pain on the left
Left side of the body and face, all sensations

q: Pressing gently on the side of your closed eye makes you see a faint ring of light, although no light enters the eye. What does this show?
options: Pressure produces light inside the eye
Pressure fires the vision pathway, which the brain reads as light
Mechanoreceptors in the eye send the signal to the somatosensory cortex instead
The optic nerve adapts to steady pressure

q: You stub your toe and feel a sharp jolt at once, then a second or so later a throbbing ache that lasts. What explains the two waves?
options: The sharp pain travels in the dorsal columns and the ache in the spinothalamic tract
The ache is referred pain from an internal organ
Fast pain runs in myelinated axons; slow pain in slower unmyelinated ones
The same axons fire twice because of the refractory period

q: Where do the spinocerebellar tracts carry proprioceptive signals?
options: To the cerebellum, on the same side, without reaching awareness
To the thalamus, then to the postcentral gyrus
To the hypothalamus, which sets body temperature
To the medulla, where they cross to the opposite cortex

q: In the trigeminal sensory pathway, where are the cell bodies of the first-order neurons?
options: In the dorsal root ganglia of the cervical nerves
In the trigeminal ganglion beside the pons

q: Which neuron is called the final common path to a skeletal muscle?
options: An upper motor neuron in the precentral gyrus
A lower motor neuron in the ventral horn
An interneuron in the dorsal horn
A neuron of the red nucleus

q: Put the corticospinal pathway for moving the right hand in order, starting in the brain.
options: Upper motor neuron in the left precentral gyrus
Lower motor neuron in the right ventral horn

q: Roughly what share of corticospinal axons cross at the pyramidal decussation?
Blood flow is cut off to a small area of the left internal capsule that carries corticospinal axons. Which side of the body becomes weak?
options: The left side of the body
The right side of the body

q: Name the pinned tract.

fig.alt: A front view of one cerebral hemisphere cut vertically, with a cross section of the spinal cord below it. Green lines (sensory) run up from the spinal cord to the cortex, with arrowheads pointing up; purple lines (motor) run down from the cortex to the spinal cord, with arrowheads pointing down. One purple line crosses to the other side before entering the cord. In the cord section, the paired green areas at the back and small green and purple areas at the sides and front mark where these bundles run. Roots leave the cord on both sides. A key reads sensory (green) and motor (purple).

q: A limb is weak and floppy, its tendon jerks are absent, its muscles have wasted over six weeks and small twitches ripple under the skin. Where is the damage most likely to be?
options: The ventral horn or ventral root
misconception: any motor damage makes muscles floppy

q: Select every finding that points to upper motor neuron damage, weeks after the injury.

Patient A cannot move the lower right side of her face, but she wrinkles her forehead normally on both sides. Patient B cannot move any part of the right side of his face, forehead included. Which statement explains the difference?
options: A: right facial nerve; B: left motor cortex
A and B: right facial nerve, worse in B
A: left motor cortex or its axons; B: right facial nerve
A: the right motor cortex or its axons; B: the left facial nerve

q: A knife wound cuts through the right half of the spinal cord at T8. Weeks later, predict the change in each finding compared with before the injury.

variables.name: Voluntary strength of the right leg
Muscle tone and tendon jerks in the right leg
Vibration and position sense in the right leg
Pain and temperature sense in the right leg
Pain and temperature sense in the left leg
Voluntary strength of the left leg

q: Blood flow stops to the arm and face area of the left primary motor cortex, and the neurons there die. Three weeks later, predict each finding compared with before.

variables.name: Strength of the right arm
Tendon jerks in the right arm
Strength of the lower right face
Strength of the right forehead
Strength of the left arm
Muscle bulk of the right arm

q: A 9-month-old baby's big toe extends upward when the outer edge of her sole is stroked. What does this mean?
options: Damage to her corticospinal tract above the lumbar cord
Damage to the lower motor neurons that supply her toes
A normal finding at her age
Weakness of the muscles that curl her toes downward

q: Which brainstem motor tract drives the antigravity extensor muscles that keep you upright when you start to tip?
In Parkinson's disease, the dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra die. Predict each change in the basal nuclei loop.

variables.name: Activity of the direct (go) pathway
Activity of the indirect (stop) pathway
Inhibition of the thalamus by the globus pallidus output
Ease of starting a movement

q: A man's right hand shakes as it nears a cup and he overshoots it, but the hand is still at rest and his grip is strong. Rapidly flipping his right hand over and back is clumsy. Where is the damage most likely to be?
Name the pinned region of the cerebellum.

fig.alt: Two drawings of the cerebellum colored by region. On the left, the cerebellum is cut down the midline beside the brainstem, showing its branching folds: the front part purple, the large back part green and a small orange lobe tucked underneath next to the brainstem. On the right, the cerebellum is drawn spread flat and seen from above, with the same colors: a bracket marks the narrow middle strip as the vermis and the broad side part as a hemisphere, and the orange flocculonodular lobe at the bottom is labeled as a central nodulus with a flocculus at each end.

q: This sequence describes how the direct pathway of the basal nuclei lets a chosen movement go ahead. Which step is wrong?
options: The motor cortex excites direct-pathway neurons of the striatum
The striatal neurons inhibit the output neurons of the globus pallidus
The globus pallidus output now inhibits the thalamus more strongly
The thalamus excites the motor cortex, and the movement goes ahead

q: Fill the gap in the cerebellum's input and output routes: signals from the spinal cord enter through the inferior cerebellar peduncle → the cortex's motor plan, relayed by the pons, enters through ______ → corrections leave through the superior cerebellar peduncle toward the thalamus.

A 58-year-old has wasting and twitching of the muscles of both hands, yet his knee jerks are brisk, both big toes go up when his soles are stroked, and sensation is normal everywhere. What best explains this mixture?
options: Damage to the dorsal columns of the cord
Damage to both upper and lower motor neurons
Damage to the peripheral nerves of both arms

q: Name the pinned structure.

fig.alt: A tall drawing following motor axons from the brain to the spinal cord. At the top, a quarter of a cerebral hemisphere cut vertically shows yellow neurons in the precentral gyrus. Their axons run down as a bundle through a slice of the midbrain, in the cerebral peduncle, then down the front of the medulla in a purple column, the pyramid. Near the bottom of the medulla most of the axons swing across the midline at the decussation of the pyramids and descend in the lateral corticospinal tract at the side of a spinal cord slice; a few continue uncrossed in the anterior corticospinal tract. In the cord, a yellow upper motor neuron ending meets a teal lower motor neuron, whose axon leaves the cord toward skeletal muscles. A key marks upper motor neurons yellow and lower motor neurons teal.

q: Put the parts of a reflex arc in the order a signal passes through them.
Fill the gap in the reflex arc: sensory receptor → sensory neuron → ____ → motor neuron → effector.

A man's left knee jerk is absent, even with reinforcement. His left thigh muscles are strong when he kicks on purpose, but he has lost feeling on the front of his left knee. Which part of the reflex arc is most likely damaged?
options: The ventral root of the lumbar segments
The dorsal root of the lumbar segments
The motor neurons in the ventral horn

q: This sequence describes the patellar reflex. One step is wrong. Find it.
options: A tap on the patellar ligament stretches the quadriceps femoris
Muscle spindles in the quadriceps fire
Sensory axons enter the cord through the dorsal roots
Interneurons relay the signal to the quadriceps motor neurons
Quadriceps motor neurons fire and the muscle contracts

q: When a clinician taps the calcaneal tendon and the foot points down, which sensory receptor detects the tap?
options: Golgi tendon organs in the calcaneal tendon
Nociceptors in the skin over the tendon
Muscle spindles in the calf muscles
Tactile corpuscles in the skin of the heel
misconception: the tendon is the sensor in a deep tendon reflex

q: Which of these depend on at least one interneuron between the sensory and motor neurons? Select all that apply.
options: Contraction of the quadriceps in the knee jerk
Relaxation of the hamstrings during the knee jerk
The tendon reflex from Golgi tendon organs

q: You step on a tack with your right foot. Predict the change in activity of each group of motor neurons in the next fraction of a second.

variables.name: Motor neurons to the right leg's flexors
Motor neurons to the right leg's extensors
Motor neurons to the left leg's extensors

It uses one motor neuron that runs all the way from the CNS to a skeletal muscle

In the upper motor neuron pathway to the right leg

In a knee jerk, the sensory path is 0.6 m at 70 m/s and the motor path is 0.6 m at 60 m/s, with about 1 ms at the central synapse and 3 ms at the muscle. A disease strips myelin from the motor axons and slows them to 30 m/s. About how long does the reflex now take?
During the knee jerk, what stops the hamstrings from contracting against the kick?
options: Spindle axons excite inhibitory interneurons that silence the hamstring motor neurons
The hamstrings are stretched too, so their own spindles relax them
Golgi tendon organs in the quadriceps fire first and switch off the hamstring motor neurons
The cortex sends a signal to relax the hamstrings before the tap

q: Name the pinned neuron.

fig.alt: Two pathways from a spinal cord cross section. Top, the autonomic efferent pathway: a myelinated axon runs from the lateral horn to a ganglion, where it synapses on a second neuron whose unmyelinated axon runs on to a curved strip of smooth muscle; an enlarged inset shows a swelling along that axon releasing transmitter onto the muscle surface. Bottom, the somatic efferent pathway: one myelinated axon runs from the ventral horn directly to a bundle of skeletal muscle fibers, and an inset shows it ending in a single synaptic terminal.
